title: Efficient monitoring of memory regions containing sensitive artifacts

source_provenance.note: Document metadata, abstract, detailed description excerpts, and claims were visible in the user-supplied capture.

classification_signals: G06F21/554 security arrangements for protecting computers

scope_model.control_loop: identify protected region -> detect access -> evaluate rule -> allow/log, delay for approval, abort, or roll back -> persist audit evidence
gpt_doug_maven_independent_mapping: treat signed runtime artifacts, credentials, policy files, and high-value configuration as protected artifacts
represent protection policy in a provenance-backed manifest
evaluate mutation policy at the software control plane before applying changes
use human approval for consequential writes
retain checkpoint or shadow state for rollback
emit audit records for both denied and permitted sensitive operations
keep detection, decision, mitigation, and audit components independently testable

publicly_described_functional_concepts: sensitive region descriptors populated with protected memory locations
security rules associated with protected regions
monitoring memory accesses from compute engines
blocking or aborting undesired memory accesses
delaying access while requesting programmatic approval
shadow-copy rollback of a disallowed change
showing monitoring configuration and statistics through programmatic interfaces
optional machine-learning or knowledge-base assistance for identifying regions to monitor

claim_scope_signals.independent_claim_theme: hardware memory-monitor circuitry uses sensitive-region descriptors to detect protected-region accesses, evaluate security rules, and initiate mitigation operations
claim_scope_signals.legal_scope_rule: Controlling claims, prosecution history, legal status, and jurisdiction-specific law require human legal review before any infringement or freedom-to-operate conclusion.

design_divergence_defaults: implement GPT-DOUG-MAVEN protection as software policy, provenance, checkpointing, and runtime supervision rather than reproducing the claimed hardware monitor
use independently defined protected-artifact identities rather than physical memory address descriptors
use existing OS, container, filesystem, signing, and policy controls as independent enforcement mechanisms
separate read observability from write authorization
require explicit human approval for destructive or consequential artifact mutations
maintain versioned rollback state and tamper-evident audit history

mandatory_safety_boundaries: fail closed on unknown protected-artifact policy
signed or hashed provenance for protected artifacts
audit every policy decision affecting protected artifacts
